paragraphs.text: See on Eze 18:1.

Fitly here compared to a goodly ship, {a} and her desolation to a dismal shipwreck. Theodoret’s note on the text is, that when we correct sinners, or threaten them, it should be done with commiseration and compassion. Here we have God’s own example for it.
paragraphs.anchor: Take up a lamentation for Tyrus.

paragraphs.text: “ Ille dolet quoties cogitur esse ferox. ”
{a} Apud Horat. Resp. navis nomine significatur. - Carm. lib. i. od. 14.
As now the city of Venice is,
paragraphs.anchor: O thou that art situated at the entry of the sea.

paragraphs.text: “ Media insuperabilis unda. ”

Environed with her embracing Neptune, to whom (as the ceremony of throwing a ring into the sea implieth, saith one) she marrieth herself with yearly nuptials. But hath she so learned Christ? and doth not the Nebuchadnezzar of Constantinople now threaten her sore?
So that nothing can be added to me: I am ocellus orbis. But who made thee to differ? Is not all thy beauty borrowed? will not this thy bulging wall down ere long?
paragraphs.anchor: Thou hast said, I am of perfect beauty.

paragraphs.text: Wherewith thou art compassed and crowned, as it were, {Isa 23:8} being half a mile distant from the continent, till first Nebuchadnezzar, and then Alexander the Great, by casting earth, wood, and stones into the sea, made of it an island, a peninsula, &c.
paragraphs.anchor: Thy borders are in the midst of the sea.

paragraphs.text: The Sidonians, saith Justin; {a} 240 years before Solomon’s temple was built, saith Josephus. {b}
{a} Lib. xviii., lib. viii.
{b} Ant., cap. 2.
Of the most precious materials, which, with thy rich freight, did incite and entice the arch-pirate to surprise and make prize of thee.
paragraphs.anchor: They have made all thy ship boards.

paragraphs.text: Those very best of the best. See Eze 27:5.

i.e., Of Greece and the Archipelago, {Gen 10:4} far set and dear bought. Benches and decks might well have been made of worse matters: sed opulentiam fere sequitur superbia, luxus, libido, &c.; wealth breeds swelth, which is a dangerous symptom, as in the body, so in the mind too.
paragraphs.anchor: Out of the isles of Chittim

paragraphs.text: “ Pulcherrima regna
Luxuries vitiis, odiisque superbia vertit. ”
- Claudian.
When coarse canvas might have served the turn as well.

Which is held to be the finest, whitest, and costliest. Oh this unnecessary bravery! Luxus est anteambulo ruinae: Luxury portends your ruin, how many hath it utterly undone! When a man shall see a cloak embroidered over with woods and parks and lordships, and lined with obligations and bonds and statutes, will not the beggar soon catch such a prodigal by the back?
i.e., Of Italy, saith the Chaldee paraphrast; of Greece, say others; the Fortunate islands, say some, which are called the Elysian islands for their pleasure and plenty.
The poop deck of thy ships. Of Cleopatra’s sumptuous ship or barge, the poop deck whereof was of gold, the oars silver, the sails purple, &c., see Plutarch in Anton.
Famous all the world over for their skill at sea and otherwise.

Wise they had need to be that sit at the stern of a state. Let them not therefore be ignorant, or idle, or otherwise faulty, lest they mar all: let them be active Argonauts. They have their names here in the Hebrew from the ropes of the ship, which they as pilots must skilfully order, shifting sails according to the wind. Counsel also, in that tongue, hath its name from the same root. {a}
paragraphs.anchor: Thy wise men were thy pilots.

paragraphs.text: {a} úçáåìä
Great architects, {1Ki 5:18} but persecutors of the Church. {Psa 83:7}
Or, Stoppers of chinks, stuppa, pice, aliaque materia, when the ship springeth a leak.
They were to thee both for muniment and for ornament.
These were not pigmies, as the Vulgate rendereth it; nor Medes, as Symmachus; nor Cappadocians, as the Chaldee paraphrast; but Syrians of a city called Gamalla, whereof see Pliny. {a}
{a} Nat. Hist., lib. ii. cap. 91.
i.e., The Carthaginians, say some; the citizens of Tarsus, another colony of the Tyrians, say others.
Heb., In thy derelictions, because they left their commodities behind them, taking others in exchange; for,
“ Non omnis fert omnia tellus. ”

i.e., Grecians, Spaniards, and Muscovites or Cappadocians, who were naturally of a servile disposition: they were anciently called Meschines, saith Josephus, {a} of Meshech, the son of Japhet. {Gen 10:2}
i.e., They bought and sold slaves, as now they do in Turkey.
paragraphs.anchor: They traded the persons of men

paragraphs.text: {a} Lib. i. cap. 6.
i.e., The Germans, saith the Targum, who are still excellent horsemen. The Jews call the Turks the house of Togarmah.
paragraphs.anchor: They of the house of Togarmah

paragraphs.text: Arabians. {Gen 10:7} The Septuagint render them Rhodians.
The elephant’s two great tusks, crooked as horns.
Hebenum, which hath affinity with Eben, which signifieth a stone, for ebony is a wood hard and heavy as a stone. The Chaldee rendereth it peacocks.
Heb., Works. The Tyrians were ingenious workmen, as Hiram, whom Solomon therefore so admired that he called him his father.
Or, Chrysoprasus, or crystal, or carbuncle, or onyx. Jerome confesseth that he knoweth not what to call it.
Where the best grew, even the kidneys of wheat, as Moses hath it. {Deu 32:14 cf. Jdg 11:33 Act 12:20}
Rosin or balsam, whereof Judea yielded the best in the whole world.

i.e., Of Aleppo, say some, famous then for wine, now for milk, whence also it hath its name, for the Turks call milk alep; and if the Via lactea Milky Way were on earth, it would be found there, saith one.
Anciently called Laish. {Jdg 18:29} Javan, or the Grecians, were great travellers. {a}
Discursatory.
“ Impiger extremos currit mercator ad Indos. ”
- Horat.
{See Trapp on "Psa 38:11"}
{a} Graecus vagabundus. - Vatab.
Heb., Clothes of freedom, such as are worn by gallants and magnificos.
Or, Saddles or trappings, ad vehiculum for carriages.
Heb., They were the merchants of thy hand, or at thy hand, for cattle could not be carried far.
paragraphs.anchor: They occupied with thee in lambs.

paragraphs.text: Merchants are as useful in a commonwealth as mechanics, for exporting and importing commodities; only they must observe the gospel standard, "Whatever ye would that men should do to you, do ye the same to them."
paragraphs.anchor: In these were they thy merchants.

paragraphs.text: i.e., Ethiopians and Indians. Erat enim Tyrus emporium propemodum totius mundi. {a}
paragraphs.anchor: The merchants of Sheba and Raamah

paragraphs.text: All aromatic wares. Pliny reports of cinnamon that in his time a pound of it was worth a thousand denarii, that is, 150 crowns of our money. Galen writeth that it was hard to be found, except in the storehouses of great princes.
{a} Oecolamp.
In Mesopotamia, or Charrae, in Parthia, where Crassus was slain.
Or, Chalne, where the tower of Babel was built nine miles high. {a}
Where paradise once was: sed periit rosa, mansit spina.
i.e., Medea, saith the paraphrast.
{a} The tower of Babel was 9164 paces from the ground.
In omnibus perfectissimis; in the very best commodities, whether for worth or workmanship.
Or, Very heavy: {a} as a ship, though not top full, may yet have freight enough to sink it; so had this metaphorical ship Tyre enough to sink it, though not enough to satisfy it.
paragraphs.anchor: Thou wast replenished and made very glorious.

paragraphs.text: {a} Aggravata es.
Narrat Tyri naufragium. Here beginneth the prophecy of Tyre’s woeful shipwreck. {a}
paragraphs.anchor: Thy rowers have brought thee into great waters.

paragraphs.text: Called the "Mariner’s misery." The Chaldees were east from Tyre, the great wealth whereof solicited their poverty to set upon them, as the wealth of Cyprus did the Romans.
{a} Omnium horum ruinam et rapinam praenunciat.
As a ship that sinketh, and cannot be buoyed up again.
paragraphs.anchor: Shall fall into the midst of the seas.

paragraphs.text: Or, The waves, or the boats which they throw out of the ship. See on Eze 26:10.
At their Conclamatum est: but why, did they then steer no better? Here we see - all covet, all loose.
paragraphs.anchor: Of the cry of thy pilots.

paragraphs.text: That have escaped to land with their lives.
paragraphs.anchor: And all that handle the oar.

Moerebunt induti saccis, inducto calvitio. If this had been for sin, as it is offensivum Dei, et aversivum a Deo, then it had been right.
An elegant mimesis.
Quae obmutuit, like her that lost her voice and life together.
Good things are fairest on the back side; the worth of them is best known by the want of them. Our eye seeth not things but at a distance.
i.e., In the overflowing of the wars. {Eze 27:26}
paragraphs.anchor: In the depths of the waters

paragraphs.text: i.e., Appalled and dispirited.
paragraphs.anchor: They shall be troubled in their countenance

paragraphs.text: Either as astonied at thee, or rather as deriding thee, {a} like as he who seeth another fall into the dirt, first pitieth him and then jeereth him. See the like, Jer 19:8; Jer 49:17.
paragraphs.anchor: The merchants shall hiss at thee.

paragraphs.text: Because God hath hanged thee up in gibbets, as it were. Or thou wast a terror once, but now a scorn.
